solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old American from main cabin calling repeatedly

definitions.note: a member of the ancient Andean civilisation of Peru

indicators.note: the answer is taken out from inside the run of words that follows
the same four letters lurk twice, across main cabin and again across cabin calling

explanation.surface: An old traveller is heard shouting again and again from the main cabin of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of 'main' and start of 'cabin', and again across the end of 'cabin' and start of 'calling', which is what 'repeatedly' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the pre-Columbian people who ruled an empire in the Andes, so one of them is an ancient native of the Americas.

clue.text: Never wrong about European's superficial appearance

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece
something wrong is out of order, so the letters of never are rearranged

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A complaint that a European never shows anything more than a shallow outward look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns NEVER into VENER, and 'about' wraps those letters around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin decorative surface layer, and figuratively a thin outward show hiding what lies beneath.

clue.text: For power, part of old aircraft that's forward

definitions.text: part of old aircraft that's forward

parts.note: to be for something is to be pro it
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Talking about engines: a piece of a vintage plane mounted at the front to give it power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For power' reads as the purpose of the part, but it is simply the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop, short for propeller, is the spinning blade at the nose of older piston-engined planes.

clue.text: Little bit inspector left, finally

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is placed last, after the detective

parts.note: Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series

explanation.surface: The inspector at last went away with only a tiny crumb.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the famous fictional Oxford detective; 'finally' tells you the L comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small piece of food or a tiny amount of anything.

clue.text: Most outstanding, could be taken for granted

parts.note: as an adverb, 'most' can mean best, as in 'the one I liked most'
a debt that is outstanding is still owed

explanation.surface: The finest thing might be something we simply assume will always be there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most outstanding' reads as one phrase meaning excellent, but it splits into two pieces; 'taken for granted' also hides the definition, 'granted'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to give or confer, so something bestowed has been granted as a gift or honour.

clue.text: A couple of extra points in Tory interpretation

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories
a version is one person's account or interpretation

explanation.surface: A political commentator notes the Conservatives gain a couple of points in some reading of the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union, kicking the ball over the bar after a try earns two further points.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a conversion is the kick after a try which, if successful, adds two points to the score.

clue.text: Where chest may be found with gold for person seeking wealth

parts.note: a chest is covered by clothing, here in a vest
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A treasure hunter looks for a chest full of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests a treasure chest, but it is the body part, found in a vest (an undershirt).
explanation.definitionFit: An investor puts money into ventures hoping it will grow, so he or she is out to make a fortune.

clue.text: Partners carried by characteristic conveyance

indicators.note: the partners are held inside the next word, as passengers are carried in a vehicle

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A couple travel in their usual vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, and North and South play as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the carrying of people or goods from place to place, and the Ford Transit is a familiar van.

clue.text: Travel north or east, at first, in this state

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed at the front, ahead of the others

parts.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east
to travel is to go
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A choice of heading north or east when setting out across this US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' moves 'or east' to the front of the answer, ahead of 'Travel north'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a US state on the Pacific coast, between California and Washington.

clue.text: Way of producing pictures occurred to artist

parts.note: an idea that came to someone occurred to them
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A painter has a new idea for how to make images.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occurred to' reads as an idea dawning on the artist, but 'occurred' is one piece and 'to' links it to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device used to take photographs, so it is a means of producing images.

clue.text: I must appear ahead of time in job I have, for certain

indicators.note: says the letter has to be put into the next word
the letter goes inside the job word, just before its abbreviation for time

parts.note: a post is a job or position
contracted, I have is I've

explanation.surface: Someone sure they must be early for the job they already hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead of time' is precise: the I goes just before the T of the job word, T being the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To be positive is to be completely sure, without doubt.

clue.text: For whom lowering weapon in trap is a dangerous act

definitions.text: For whom lowering weapon in trap is a dangerous act

parts.words: For whom lowering weapon in trap is a dangerous act
parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, so the weapon is lowered down the throat as a circus stunt

explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' suggests a snare or ambush; here it is slang for mouth, and the 'act' is a performance, not a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: This performer passes a blade down the throat and gullet as a fairground or circus feat.

clue.text: Comedian with point on TV as place for swearing, initially

parts.note: a wit is a person known for clever humour
a ness is a headland or point, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness
the box is British slang for television

explanation.surface: A comic appears on television with a joke that ends in swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In court a witness swears the oath on first entering the box, which is why the definition says 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British courtroom the enclosure where a witness stands to take the oath and give evidence.

clue.text: Man supporting a vote that's assumed to be valid

indicators.note: in a down answer, the last piece sits below and holds up the others

parts.note: a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone backing a ballot assumed to be legitimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM, sitting under A and X in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as true without proof, a starting assumption.

clue.text: Astonish trio in front of VW heading north

parts.note: in the alphabet the three letters coming just before V and W

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word north

explanation.surface: Three people standing before a Volkswagen driving north amaze onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: VW looks like the car maker, but it is two letters of the alphabet; the three letters before them are S, T, U.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or amaze them so they are left speechless.

clue.text: Corruptly earning income primarily from part of Africa

indicators.note: done crookedly, so the letters are mixed up
the first letter of the word income

explanation.surface: Someone makes money dishonestly, chiefly from a region of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The I from 'income' joins EARNING before 'Corruptly' rearranges them all together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigerian describes a person or thing from Nigeria, the West African country.

clue.text: Ponder, making most of the writer's material

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: ink is what a writer uses

explanation.surface: Reflect while getting the best out of an author's fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the last letter from 'the' to leave TH; 'material' is not cloth but the writer's ink.
explanation.definitionFit: To think about something is to consider it carefully, to mull it over.

clue.text: Good-natured socialist family

parts.note: a kind person is good-natured
red is the traditional colour and nickname for a socialist

explanation.surface: A friendly left-wing household.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred are one's relatives, the people related by blood.

clue.text: Cut flower for stage

indicators.note: the end of the flower's name is chopped off

parts.note: a daisy is a common flower

explanation.surface: A trimmed bloom placed for display on a platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut flower' looks like a florist's bouquet; 'Cut' loses the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform at the end of a hall, for speakers or honoured guests.

clue.text: Indication of forthcoming match in fight arena

parts.note: an engagement is a battle or clash with an enemy
a ring is an arena for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: Promotion of an upcoming bout in a boxing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sporting contest, but it means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring given when a couple become betrothed signals a wedding to come.

clue.text: Spirits provided by good landlords

parts.note: a pub landlord is the host who serves guests

explanation.surface: Drinks supplied by kindly publicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' looks like drink served by the landlords; here it means phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts are the spirits of the dead said to appear to the living.

clue.text: Criminal activity that's skilfully handled in court

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fraudulent scheme for making money
second meaning: the strung bat used on a tennis or squash court

explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court after 'Criminal activity'; it is a tennis or squash court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dishonest scheme to make money and the bat used in tennis and squash.

clue.text: Generating lots of interest, it makes us inquisitive, first off

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for inquisitive is dropped

parts.note: curious means inquisitive

explanation.surface: Something fascinating makes us want to know more, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' sounds like curiosity; it means the charges on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurious lending charges extortionate rates on money lent.

clue.text: Recalled country in Asia, monarchy

definitions.note: a country known by this name in the past, now renamed

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Remembering a kingdom in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' looks like a reversal signal, but the letters run forwards; it says the country is a remembered one.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam was the official name of Thailand until 1939, so it is a nation of the past.

clue.text: Top performance in form

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the best result ever achieved

explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' reads as an athlete performing well; 'form' is a separate meaning, a person's past history.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the best achievement yet set and a list of someone's previous convictions or results.

clue.text: Shake foundation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sway or disturb violently
second meaning: a firm base, as solid stone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to sway or shock someone, and solid ground on which something stands firm.

clue.text: Work shown in section for modern paintings

indicators.note: the work is displayed inside the section

parts.note: a part is a section
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A painting displayed in a gallery's contemporary room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a musical or literary opus, which crosswords shorten to its usual catalogue abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop art is the 1950s-60s movement drawing on consumer imagery, as with Warhol and Lichtenstein.

clue.text: People watching interview

definitions.meaning: first meaning: spectators at a show
second meaning: a formal meeting with an important person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both spectators of a performance and a formal hearing granted by a monarch or dignitary.
